title: Public technical disclosure of AI implementation in finance: Python-framed evidence from 253 NYSE-listed financial companies
summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) claims in public markets increasingly raise disclosure, comparability, and investor-protection questions, yet evidence on how listed financial firms publicly describe implementation remains fragmented and difficult to compare. This study examines public technical disclosure rather than internal adoption by constructing a screened, exchange-bounded corpus for 253 NYSE-listed financial companies. The source intake contained 554 rows; six exact repeated rows were removed before screening, leaving 548 screened rows. The 505-sentence extended analysis corpus combines a 253-sentence firm-anchor layer with a 252-sentence direct-verification layer; the remaining issuer is retained in the direct-verification audit as a closed unit with no strict direct match. Firms are coded into three disclosure states: explicit Python, indirect AI, and none, and the corpus is used to map subsector profiles, channel location, and the rarity of quantified public outcome claims through an outcome claims index (OCI). The results show that 34 firms (13.4%) are classified as Explicit Python, 216 (85.4%) as Indirect AI, and 3 (1.2%) as None. Explicit Python naming is uneven across subsectors and is concentrated mainly in employment materials and technical documentation rather than in filings or investor-facing channels. The public technical surface is therefore real but thin: firms more often signal implementation orientation than disclose a detailed tool stack. Quantified public outcome claims are rarer still, with five OCI-positive firms and five OCI-positive sentences (1.98% of firms). These findings indicate that public financial-sector communication is much stronger on AI-related implementation signals than on measurable outcomes. The paper offers a reproducible disclosure map for a bounded listed firm population and a framework for distinguishing general AI language, implementation-specific technical naming, and quantified public claims in regulated capital market settings.

title: Greening the Chain: Supplier Emission Reductions From Focal Firm Green Bonds
summary: ABSTRACT Green bonds have emerged as a significant financial instrument for sustainable development. Grounded in stakeholder theory, institutional theory, and signaling theory, this study contributes to the sustainable development literature by exploring how focal firms' green bond issuance influences green supply chain sustainable governance. Using 2132 firm‐year observations of Chinese A‐share listed firms during 2016–2023, the study employs a fixed‐effects model to examine the relationship between focal firms' green bond issuance and supplier carbon emissions. The empirical results indicate that focal firms' green bond issuance reduces supplier carbon emissions, with supplier green innovation and analyst attention serving as two key mediating mechanisms. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis reveals that this emission reduction effect is more pronounced for suppliers that are state‐owned, smaller, or operating in more competitive industries. This study reveals the broader environmental governance effects of green bonds from the perspective of suppliers, providing practical implications for government green finance policy formulation and corporate supply chain decarbonization strategies.

title: Conceptualising Digital Transformation Through Recursive Capability Constriction: Evidence from Australian NDIS Providers
summary: Digital transformation is a strategic priority across care-intensive service sectors, yet many organisations struggle to realise its intended benefits. Existing research often examines technological, organisational, and environmental barriers separately, offering limited insight into their interconnections within organisational systems. Drawing on Systems Theory and Sociotechnical Systems (STS) Theory, this study investigates digital transformation among small and medium providers within Australia’s National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). Using an interpretive qualitative design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 participants from 15 distinct NDIS provider organisations in Sydney, Australia, followed by reflexive thematic analysis and systems-oriented interpretation. Participants described recurring associations among technological misalignment, fragmented software, adaptive workarounds, increased administrative demands, and constraints on organisational capacity for digital improvement, with regulatory and resource pressures interacting with these technological and organisational conditions. Building on these cross-sectional patterns, this study develops Recursive Capability Constriction (RCC), a systems-based conceptual framework that proposes how technological misalignment, compensatory adaptation, administrative expansion, and constrained organisational capability for digital improvement may become interconnected through reinforcing relationships. Rather than representing an inevitable or empirically established causal sequence, RCC provides a conditional explanation of how local adaptations may become associated with constraints on subsequent digital improvement. By shifting attention from isolated implementation barriers to interconnected sociotechnical relationships, RCC extends digital transformation research and provides practical guidance for managing digital change in regulated care environments.

title: Emerging Resistance in the Digital Transformation of Public Transport: Older Passengers With Dementia and Experiences of Ecobiographical Disruption
summary: ABSTRACT The digital transformation of public transport is prone to resistance. Among the discontents of such transformation, older people and those living with cognitive impairments are repeatedly identified. Stereotypes assuming their innate resistance to technological change are widespread, but research shows that older people with dementia can have rich digital lives. This paper reports findings from an ethnography of public transport digital transformation with older passengers living with dementia in Greater Manchester, UK. Combining interviews, photography, poetry, route maps and contextual statistics, four cases illustrate the emergence of resistance to digital displays, cashless exchange, e‐ticketing and live routing. They reveal subtle, nuanced and contextually contingent resistances that emerge from digital transformation disrupting passenger ecobiographies—the rootedness of their lives in longstanding ecosystems. Findings show that everyday resistance can be small, transient and relational, and should be taken seriously as an indicator of potential injustices. Future initiatives should meaningfully include older and disabled users throughout to increase alertness to ecobiographical disruption and emerging resistance.

title: TRANSGENDER EMPLOYMENT LAW AND WORKPLACE INCLUSION IN CORPORATE INDIA
summary: The translation of constitutional guarantees into substantive professional reality remains a critical frontier for corporate governance frameworks and digital economy landscapes in India. This article focuses on the socio-economic status of transgender professionals in Corporate India, analysing the shift in structure from an inflexible biological binary system to a flexible legal structure. Though the early landmark judgments placed gender identity within the Fundamental Rights of Part III of the Indian Constitution, applying such mandates to the organizational context of private firms continues to create a gap between the progressive legislation and existing procedural practices. This analysis reviews the regulatory framework of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, alongside the changes introduced by the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026.This examination will focus on judicial guidelines for substantive reasonable accommodation that have been defined by the apex court. The study considers the structural obstacles labour laws, organizational compliance mechanisms and takes the discussion beyond superficial measures of diversity and explains how private sector entities can incorporate equity into their structures to realize the constitutional transformation of dignity, equality, and economic justice in the organized labour sectors of the country. Keywords: Corporate governance frameworks, Fundamental rights, Transgender Persons Act, organizational compliance mechanisms, Economic justice

title: Capital Market Reaction to the April 2025 Trading Halt on ESG Leaders Stocks
summary: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh kebijakan Trading Halt yang diterapkan Bursa Efek Indonesia pada 8 April 2025 sebagai respons atas penurunan tajam Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan akibat tekanan eksternal, seperti ketegangan geopolitik kawasan dan pengetatan kebijakan moneter Amerika Serikat. Peristiwa tersebut diduga mengandung muatan informasi yang dapat memengaruhi perilaku investor, yang tercermin melalui Abnormal Return, Trading Volume Activity, dan Bid-Ask Spread. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji ada tidaknya perbedaan ketiga indikator tersebut sebelum dan sesudah peristiwa Trading Halt pada emiten yang tergabung dalam indeks IDX ESG Leaders. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain event study digunakan terhadap tiga puluh perusahaan yang dipilih melalui purposive sampling, diamati selama lima belas hari bursa yang terdiri atas tujuh hari sebelum, satu hari peristiwa, dan tujuh hari sesudah tanggal 8 April 2025. Data sekunder berupa harga penutupan harian, volume perdagangan, serta harga bid dan ask diperoleh dari Bursa Efek Indonesia. Pengujian hipotesis dilakukan melalui statistik deskriptif, uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk, uji Wilcoxon signed rank, dan paired sample t-test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan terdapat perbedaan Abnormal Return dan Trading Volume Activity yang signifikan, sementara Bid-Ask Spread tidak menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa peristiwa Trading Halt mengandung informasi yang direspons investor melalui perubahan harga dan aktivitas perdagangan, tanpa mengubah secara berarti tingkat likuiditas saham berbasis ESG.

title: Beyond compliance: environmental regulation and corporate responsible innovation
summary: As technological innovation increasingly generates social and environmental externalities, understanding how environmental regulation shapes corporate responsible innovation has become an important yet underexplored issue. Using panel data from Chinese A-share non-financial listed companies spanning 2011–2023, this study aims to empirically examine the impact of environmental regulation on corporate responsible innovation. The results show that environmental regulation significantly promotes corporate responsible innovation, suggesting that regulatory pressure functions not only as a compliance constraint but also as a driver of responsible innovation. Further analyses reveal that this relationship is mediated by corporate reputation, market power, and ESG performance, and green innovation quality and supply chain risk further strengthen this relationship. This study extends the literature on the institutional drivers of responsible innovation, provides valuable insights into how environmental governance can promote innovation that is ethically acceptable, socially desirable, and environmentally sustainable, and offers important implications for policymakers seeking to foster responsible innovation.

title: Human Capital to National Competitiveness: Talent Management in India’s IT Sector by 2047
summary: India’s aspiration to emerge as a developed nation by 2047 hinges critically on the evolution of its digital economy, with the Information Technology (IT) sector at its core. India’s rapidly growing digital economy and IT industry have greatly increased the need for skilled employees. Therefore, talent management has become very important for the growth of both organisations and the country. This study focuses on the main processes of talent management such as recruitment, employee growth, employee engagement, employee retention, leadership development, and workforce diversity. The research is based on secondary data collected from government reports, industrial reports, different research papers, and policy documents. The study analyses the main factors that affect talent management, such as new government policies, technological changes, workforce diversity, employee well-being, educational reforms, and the continuous need to learn new skills. Along with this, the study also examines the role of government initiatives like Skill India, Digital India, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), and the National Education Policy, which help in reducing skill gaps and increasing employment opportunities. The conclusion states that effective and inclusive talent management is not only important for the growth of the IT sector but also necessary for India’s social, economic, and technological development. A future-ready, skilled, and continuously learning workforce will help India achieve its Vision 2047 goals and make the country a leading nation in the global digital economy.

title: Exploring Research Trends in Sustainable Entrepreneurial Ecosystems: A Bibliometric Study
summary: The sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem (SEE) has emerged at the intersection of entrepreneurship, sustainability, innovation and institutional development, yet its intellectual structure and thematic evolution remain fragmented. This study integrates bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review (SLR) of 722 Scopus-indexed publications. Citation, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling and science-mapping techniques were applied using VOSviewer, complemented by systematic thematic synthesis. Findings reveal limited early research, substantial growth from 2014 and rapid expansion after 2020, reaching 196 publications in 2024. The United States leads in publications and citations, while Giuseppina Passiante is the most cited author and Christina Theodoraki demonstrates strong network connectivity. The SLR identifies nine interconnected themes covering sustainable entrepreneurship, entrepreneurial ecosystems, institutional support, collaborative innovation, digital sustainability, social inclusion, circular economy and entrepreneurship education. Overall, SEE research is shifting from conceptual ecosystem foundations towards collaborative, digital, circular and sustainability-oriented perspectives. Key research gaps concern contextual differences, Global North–South comparisons, sustainable finance, digital inclusion, ecosystem collaboration and measurable sustainability outcomes.

title: Economic Trade and Atmospheric Transport in Shaping China’s Nitrogen Deposition Patterns
summary: Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition in China is driven not only by local emissions but also by global economic demand and transboundary atmospheric transport. Unraveling these dual influences is critical for effective environmental governance. Here, we integrate an economic-emission analysis with a high-resolution atmospheric chemical transport model to quantify, for the first time, the distinct roles of domestic consumption, international trade, and atmospheric transport in shaping China’s nitrogen deposition patterns. We find that domestic consumption is the dominant contributor, responsible for 67.6% of the total deposition, involving a substantial interprovincial transfer of emissions from affluent coastal provinces to less developed inland regions. International trade attributes 7.8% of China’s deposition to foreign consumption, primarily driven by demand from the USA and Western Europe. In contrast, trans-national atmospheric transport directly accounts for 12.8%, with a disproportionately high impact on ecologically sensitive western China. Natural sources contribute the remaining 11.8%. Our results reveal a complex web of drivers extending beyond China’s borders. Mitigating nitrogen deposition, therefore, requires moving beyond local emission controls to embrace consumption-based accountability and enhanced international cooperation on both trade and atmospheric pollution to protect vulnerable ecosystems.

title: Effect of Digital Sensing Capability on Competitive Advantage of Commercial Banks in Kenya
summary: The purpose of the study was to examine the relationship between digital sensing capability and competitive advantage among commercial banks in Kenya. The study adopted a post-positivist research philosophy and an explanatory research design anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory. The target population consisted of 370 respondents drawn from the 37 commercial banks in Kenya. Stratified random sampling was employed to select 192 respondents, comprising Chief Executive Officers and Heads of key departments, including finance, marketing, human resource, strategy, customer relations, operations, credit, information and communication technology, risk and compliance, and internal audit. Primary data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire and analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics with the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25. Descriptive statistics included frequencies, means, and standard deviations, while ordinal logistic regression was used for hypothesis testing. Digital Sensing Capability was positively and significantly associated with higher Competitive Advantage (β = 6.932, SE = 0.817, Wald = 71.988, p < .001). The Nagelkerke Pseudo R² was 0.749, indicating a substantial improvement in model fit relative to the intercept-only model. This value is reported as a pseudo-R² index and is not interpreted as a percentage of variance explained, because pseudo-R² does not have the same meaning as R² in ordinary least-squares regression. Higher Digital Sensing Capability was associated with greater odds of higher Competitive Advantage. Commercial banks should continuously strengthen digital infrastructure, monitor customer behaviour and fintech developments, and use market intelligence to anticipate emerging opportunities and threats. Consistent with Dynamic Capabilities Theory, continually renewing digital sensing capabilities enables banks to adapt rapidly and sustain competitive advantage. Managers should implement structured digital sensing frameworks that integrate market, technology, and internal sensing into strategic planning to enhance competitive advantage among commercial banks in Kenya.

title: Socio-Environmental Controversies in Chile’s Peatland Governance: From Global Climate Discourses to Local Extractivist Realities
summary: This article analyzes the legislative process that culminated in Chile’s 2024 Peatland Protection Law (Law 21.660), employing critical discourse analysis to examine the parliamentary debates that shaped this regulatory framework. Unlike previous studies on environmental governance in Chile—which have focused on identifying specific conflicts, characterizing extractivist patterns, or diagnosing institutional fragility—this work exposes the socio-technical controversies underlying peatland governance. It demonstrates how global climate commitments (NDCs) articulate with—and often clash with—local extractivist realities, offering an analysis of peatland governance at the intersection of legal regulation, ecological knowledge, and political economy.The study shows that environmental legislation does not emerge solely from scientific or political consensus, but from contentious negotiations in which knowledge, power, and economic interests are co-produced. The analysis identifies three central axes of controversy: the strategic mobilization of scientific knowledge; the negotiation of legal frameworks around conservation and regulated extraction; and the institutional compromises through which sustainability is translated into policy under unequal conditions of power and oversight.The Chilean case illustrates how a regulatory process, such as the construction of a climate agenda, is subject to controversial dynamics, which relativize the characteristics of local economies and socio-ecological dynamics, thereby generating weaknesses in normative strength. The article contributes to debates on environmental governance by demonstrating the limits of implementing Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) when global commitments encounter entrenched power relations and unequal regulatory capacity.

title: Artificial Intelligence Disruption and Structural Enrollment Decline in Economics and Business Higher Education: Longitudinal Evidence from Indonesia
summary: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation, and technology-driven economic systems has fundamentally reshaped global higher education dynamics, particularly within conventional economics and business programs. This study investigates the phenomenon of structural enrollment decline in economics and business higher education during the artificial intelligence era through a longitudinal institutional analysis of the Accounting and Management study programs at STIE Mulia Pratama, Indonesia, over the 1998–2025 period. Employing a quantitative longitudinal approach, the study utilizes institutional enrollment data obtained from the Indonesian Higher Education Database (PDDIKTI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, trend analysis, linear regression, forecasting analysis, and interpretative analysis to identify long-term enrollment transformation and institutional sustainability challenges. The findings reveal three major enrollment phases consisting of growth, fluctuation, and persistent structural decline. Regression analysis confirms statistically significant negative enrollment trends within both study programs. The Accounting program experienced an average annual decline of 3.356 students, while the Management program demonstrated a stronger annual decline of 5.056 students, indicating higher vulnerability to technological disruption and changing educational preferences. The study further reveals that AI disruption, employability orientation, digital economic transformation, and competency-based educational preferences substantially influence educational decision-making among younger generations. Consequently, conventional economics and business education increasingly faces sustainability challenges associated with declining institutional attractiveness and labor market transformation. This study contributes to the higher education literature by positioning declining enrollment as a manifestation of structural transformation rather than temporary institutional fluctuation. The integration of longitudinal institutional evidence, AI disruption perspectives, and sustainability analysis provides a broader analytical framework for understanding the future challenges of higher education within the digital economy era.

title: CEO Ideologically (In)Congruent Activism and Investor Reactions: An Attribution of CEO Intentions Perspective
summary: Abstract The phenomenon of chief executive officers (CEOs) taking activism stances on contested sociopolitical issues is increasing, yet it remains unclear how observing investors discern CEO intentions behind activism engagements, thereby shaping their judgments and subsequent reactions. By relaxing the assumption that CEO activism is an unabashed expression of personal beliefs, we propose the concept of CEO ideologically (in)congruent activism and develop a framework wherein investors may attribute CEO intentions underlying incongruent (versus congruent) activism engagements as more organization‐driven (versus self‐driven) interest pursuits, thereby leading to more positive investor evaluations and reactions. Furthermore, we argue that the positive effect of CEO ideologically incongruent activism on investor reactions will be amplified when the CEO owns a higher level of stock ownership but weakened when the firm receives a greater corporate social responsibility (CSR) rating. We corroborate our propositions using a sample of CEO activism events for S&P 500 firms from 2012 to 2021. Our findings demonstrate the heterogeneity and critical influence of CEO intentions behind activism engagements and shed light on how investors integrate multi‐informational cues when evaluating and reacting to managerial incongruent behaviours.

title: Leadership as a human-systems capability: A mixed-method exploration of environmental consciousness and green innovative behavior
summary: This study examines how transformational and benevolent leadership foster green innovative behavior in hospitality organizations through environmental consciousness and leadership expectations. Using a sequential exploratory mixed-method design, Study 1 conducted semi-structured interviews with hospitality employees and applied thematic analysis to identify how leadership shapes sustainability engagement. Study 2 tested the resulting model using partial least squares structural equation modeling with survey data from hospitality employees. The qualitative findings identified five mechanisms: vision-based sustainability encouragement, care-based sustainability support, environmental meaning and personal accountability, green-oriented innovative action, and expectation-based activation of action. The quantitative findings showed that transformational and benevolent leadership influenced environmental consciousness and green innovative behavior. Environmental consciousness partially mediated both leadership pathways, while leadership expectations strengthened the relationship between environmental consciousness and green innovative behavior. This study contributes to human systems research by positioning green innovation as a leadership-cognition-expectation process shaped by organizational conditions rather than individual disposition alone.

title: Mapping the Intellectual Structure of Sustainable Development Goals Research: A Bibliometric Science‐Mapping Analysis (2015–2025)
summary: ABSTRACT Since their adoption in 2015, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have become a central framework shaping global sustainability research, policy, and practice. However, SDG scholarship remains fragmented across disciplines, themes, and geographical contexts, limiting understanding of its intellectual structure and thematic evolution. This study addresses this gap through a bibliometric science‐mapping analysis of SDG research published between 2015 and July 2025. Following a PRISMA‐guided selection process, 5425 Scopus‐indexed articles published in ABDC‐ranked journals were analyzed using Bibliometrix, Biblioshiny (R), and VOSviewer. The analysis included performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, collaboration networks, thematic evolution, and strategic mapping. The findings show sustained growth in SDG research, with an annual publication growth rate of 41.21%. China, the United Kingdom, and India were the leading contributors, while the Journal of Cleaner Production was the most influential outlet. Thematic analysis shows a shift from broad sustainability discussions toward more specialized topics, including renewable energy, circular economy, artificial intelligence, and ESG‐related research. The results also reveal geographical and disciplinary disparities, particularly the limited representation of low‐income regions within the analyzed literature. This study contributes by mapping the intellectual structure, thematic development, and collaborative dynamics of SDG research over the past decade. The findings offer useful guidance for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to identify emerging priorities, research gaps, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross‐regional collaboration toward the 2030 SDG agenda.

title: From Promise to Practice in Digital Sustainability for Agro-Food Systems: A Systematic Review
summary: Digital technologies are widely promoted as solutions for sustainable agro-food systems, yet their transition from promise to practice remains uneven and poorly understood. Persistent governance, economic, and managerial barriers continue to constrain the realisation of digital sustainability, and these barriers have not been systematically synthesised. This systematic review synthesises evidence from 16 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2026, identified through a structured search of the Scopus database. Studies were included if they examined digital innovations, economic instruments, or managerial governance in agricultural or livestock systems and reported outcomes related to sustainability, resource efficiency, or adoption. A narrative synthesis approach was used to integrate findings across three interconnected pillars: economic instruments, technological innovations, and governance factors. The review finds that digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, remote sensing, the Internet of Things, and blockchain can improve productivity, resource efficiency, and predictive accuracy. However, sustainability gains depend on supportive institutional frameworks, financial mechanisms, and governance capacity. Environmental taxes and supply chain finance innovations promote low-carbon transitions, but their effectiveness hinges on digital governance infrastructure and farmer trust. Economies of scale mediate the relationship between smart farming technologies and carbon efficiency, while government regulation positively moderates this pathway. Persistent barriers include data ownership disputes, privacy concerns, weak institutional capacity, and uneven digital infrastructure. Evidence is concentrated in Asia and Europe and relies heavily on simulation-based studies, limiting generalisability. Moving from promise to practice requires integrated governance, economic incentives, and institutional capacity building. Policymakers should prioritise trust-reinforcing data governance, progressive financing schemes, and rural digital infrastructure to enable inclusive and resilient agro-food systems.

title: The carbon reduction effect evaluation of technology-finance pilot policy: evidence from 226 Chinese cities
summary: Balancing economic growth with carbon emission reduction lies at the core of China’s ‘dual carbon’ goals. This study investigates the carbon abatement effects and influencing mechanisms of the technology-finance pilot policy (TFPP). Using panel data for 226 cities over 2010–2022, the study calculates urban carbon emission efficiency (CEE) via the SBM model and evaluates policy effects using the multi-period difference-in-differences model and Spatial Durbin Model. The study’s datasets and the findings are available from the corresponding author as follows. First, the TFPP significantly improves urban CEE, accompanied by an evident spatial spillover effect, a conclusion that remains valid after a series of robustness tests. Second, mechanism analysis identifies three transmission channels: lowering energy consumption intensity, upgrading industrial structure, and boosting green innovation. Third, the policy effects are more pronounced in eastern regions, large cities and resource-based cities. Differentiated implementation strategies for the TFPP are therefore proposed, including strengthened regional coordinated carbon reduction and improved financial support capacity in non-pilot regions. This paper clarifies influences, heterogeneity and spatial spillover effects of the TFPP on CEE, and provides policy implications for regional collaborative governance.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Corporate Energy Efficiency: A Pathway to Sustainable Manufacturing—Evidence from Chinese Firms
summary: In the context of global efforts to achieve sustainable development and carbon neutrality, improving industrial energy efficiency has become a cornerstone of green transformation. This study examines how corporate AI-related disclosure intensity is associated with sustainable energy efficiency in manufacturing firms. Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2012 to 2024, we measure corporate energy efficiency using energy intensity based on standard coal. AI-related disclosure intensity is constructed from the frequency of AI-related terms in firms’ annual reports and logarithmically transformed. Based on panel regression, process innovation association analysis, moderation analysis, and ownership-based subgroup analysis, this study finds that AI-related disclosure intensity is negatively associated with energy intensity. Higher AI-related disclosure intensity is also linked to a higher share of process innovation, indicating enhanced attention to production process improvement. Data element utilization weakens the negative association between AI-related disclosure intensity and energy intensity, suggesting a moderating effect. The negative relationship persists across both state-owned and non-state-owned firms. These findings contribute to the understanding of how AI-related disclosure intensity reflects corporate energy management and promotes sustainable manufacturing. They offer actionable implications for firms and policymakers seeking to advance green innovation and achieve a sustainable economy.

title: CYBER LAW IN INDIA: OVERVIEW AND RECENT TRENDS
summary: From a simple law on technological facilitation, India's cyber law has grown to a multi-layered system that regulates cybersecurity, data, and digital responsibility. This is all the more important for companies, citizens, and professionals that want to operate within India's digital economy. It is vital to have an idea of the cyber law development and future trends.

title: From digital transformation to corporate R&D innovation investment: largest shareholder ownership and data asset information disclosure as parallel boundary conditions
summary: Digital transformation is associated with greater R&D investment, but the ownership and disclosure conditions surrounding this relationship remain less clear. This study examines largest shareholder ownership and data asset information disclosure as two distinct moderators, using 35,954 firm-year observations from 4,388 Chinese A-share listed firms over 2009–2024. Firm and year fixed-effects models show a positive association between digital transformation and R&D innovation investment. In the baseline model, this association is stronger when the largest shareholder holds a greater equity stake and firms disclose more information about their data assets. The positive association between digital transformation and R&D investment persists across alternative measures and lagged specifications, whereas the moderation findings are more sensitive to model specification and sample restrictions. The ownership interaction weakens under stricter fixed effects, and neither interaction is statistically significant in the dynamic specification that includes lagged R&D investment. Instrumental-variable estimates are positive but imprecise and do not establish causality. These findings place ownership structure and data-related disclosure alongside technological change in explaining firms’ R&D commitments. They support a conditional account of the digital transformation–R&D relationship, while leaving the underlying monitoring and financing mechanisms open to further investigation.

title: New Quality Productive Forces and Pollution–Carbon Reduction Synergy: Evidence from Chinese Manufacturing Firms
summary: Against the background of China simultaneously pursuing the dual strategic goals of “fundamental improvement in ecological environment quality” and “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality,” exploring whether new quality productive forces—as a new engine for high-quality economic development—can effectively foster pollution–carbon reduction synergies has become a critical and urgent issue. Based on a panel dataset of Chinese A-share manufacturing listed firms spanning from 2010 to 2023, this study empirically examines the impact of new quality productive forces on enterprise pollution–carbon reduction synergy efficiency (Synergy) by integrating a super-efficiency Slack-Based Measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs, the entropy weight method (EWM), and a two-way fixed effects model. The results reveal that NPI significantly enhances corporate synergy efficiency, a finding that remains robust after addressing lagged effects, winsorization of extreme values, and potential endogeneity issues. Mechanism analysis indicates that green technological innovation (GTI) and energy efficiency (EE) enhancement serve as two vital transmission channels driving these synergistic gains. Heterogeneity analysis further discloses that NPI’s promoting effect is more pronounced among high-pollution-intensity and high-carbon-intensity enterprises, implying that firms under greater environmental governance pressure with broader scope for green transformation capture higher marginal environmental returns from NPI development. By expanding the environmental impacts of NPI from isolated pollution or carbon abatement to synergistic governance, this study provides firm-level empirical evidence for the green and low-carbon transition of the manufacturing sector, as well as practical insights for designing and implementing differentiated environmental policies.

title: Beyond Digital Infrastructure: Telecommunications Service-Market Development and Energy Carbon Intensity in Chinese Cities
summary: As digitalisation reshapes economic coordination and governance, the role of telecommunications services extends beyond network construction and ICT access. However, the environmental relevance of the activity of the telecommunications service market is not understood sufficiently. Drawing on panel data for 269 cities at the Chinese prefecture level from 2006 to 2022, this study estimates fixed-effect models and conducts a series of robustness tests to alleviate potential endogeneity and specification concerns. The results show that telecommunications service-market development (TMD) is significantly negatively associated with urban energy carbon intensity. Specifically, the baseline estimate indicates that a one-unit increase in logged TMD is associated with approximately a 0.835-unit reduction in carbon intensity. However, it is positively associated with per-capita CO2 emissions, while its association with total CO2 emissions is statistically insignificant. This relationship is robust to alternative measurements, model specifications, and endogeneity treatment. Moreover, both carbon intensity and TMD exhibit significant spatial dependence, and the main Spatial Durbin Model yields direct and indirect effects of −0.483 and −8.842, respectively, indicating negative spatial spillovers across cities. The moderation results further show that higher levels of digital economy development and fiscal decentralization significantly attenuate the negative association between TMD and energy carbon intensity in the interaction models. These results extend research on ICT development, digital infrastructure, digital economy, and low-carbon development by shifting attention from telecommunications infrastructure to TMD as a market-based information-service condition.

title: The advice guidance boundary review and targeted support – the challenges of addressing the “advice gap”
summary: Purpose Under its Advice Guidance Boundary Review (AGBR) initiative, the Financial Conduct Authority has introduced “targeted support”, a new regime that has become the focal point of a proposed “continuum of support” being developed through the AGBR. It is expected targeted support will be a significant initiative in addressing the UK’s ongoing and persistent “advice gap” in retail financial services. The purpose of this paper is to set out the regulatory framework for targeted support and consider the issues facing its successful delivery. Design/methodology/approach Twenty semi-structured interviews were conducted with a range of senior industry experts from fintechs, large platforms and financial services providers, industry bodies and independent financial advice firms. Findings This research finds that targeted support is considered an innovative approach to addressing the advice gap, and one which most in the financial services sector view positively. However, its implementation is not without challenges, including potential difficulties in processing or obtaining data, managing consumer expectations and engagement, and mitigating the potential for consumer exploitation. Originality/value The paper provides a critical assessment, based on informed industry perspectives, of a new and innovative regulatory reform. It identifies key supply-side issues facing providers of targeted support as well as the demand-side issues confronting financial consumers who may be the recipients of targeted support.

title: Corporate citizenship as a form of strategic communications
summary: Corporate citizenship as a strategic communications form under the conditions of the modern crisis of public trust to information and institutes is reviewed. The topic relevance is due to stakeholders’ growing expectations to business social role and the necessity of overcoming the gap between corporate citizenship declarative principles and its perception as a greenwashing instrument. The goal of the article is to reveal the essence of corporate citizenship as a strategic communicative practice. Such objectives as the analysis of CSR and corporate citizenship definitions, revealing its communicative functions and development of its integration to social communications system are reviewed. Based on works of Russian and foreign authors’ works the key characteristics of strategic communications are outlined, their systematic and value-oriented nature is stressed. Special attention is paid to the relationship of corporate social responsibility and corporate citizenship, and its principles, i.e. extended responsibility beyond the core business, interactive communication with communities, going beyond compliance, and the new added-value formation. The author comes to the conclusion that corporate citizenship, operated on the highest discretion level of responsibility, is not the tactic instrument, but the strategic form of communications. Corporate citizenship promotes value-oriented networks with business stakeholders, increases company competitiveness and harmonizes its relations with society, providing the foundation to long-term trust.

title: Механизмы трансформации и управления предпринимательским университетом в условиях цифровой экономики
summary: The article examines the management of an entrepreneurial university in the digital economy. It aims to summarize the key characteristics of this university model and identify approaches that can improve management effectiveness. The study is based on the analysis and synthesis of academic literature; a comparative method is used to examine different generations of university models. The analysis identifies the main characteristics of an entrepreneurial university: the integration of education, research and innovation; the practical application of knowledge; the development of entrepreneurial competencies; and cooperation with external partners. The article considers strategic, innovative, project-based and ecosystem approaches to management, as well as the use of digital technologies. It concludes that digital tools can improve management effectiveness when integrated into the university's overall processes and supported by the development of staff competencies. The article's findings may inform efforts to improve the management of higher education institutions.

title: Sustainable Competitive Intelligence for Digital Enterprise Modernization: Financial Resilience, Ensure Financial Security, and Inclusion
summary: Purpose: To examine the relationship between the digital modernization of Ukrainian enterprises and their innovation capacity, financial security, and inclusive economic development during 2021–2025. Methodology/Approach: The study used a secondary empirical desk-based approach based on open-access statistical databases, analytical reports, enterprise financial data, and economic indicators. Four clusters were analyzed: enterprise digitalization, innovation capacity, financial security and resilience, and inclusive development. Originality/Relevance: The research provides a comprehensive assessment of the effects of digital modernization on enterprise development and economic recovery in Ukraine. Key Findings: Enterprise digitalization showed the highest mean normalized value (0.63), while financial security and resilience reached 0.57, recovering from 0.36 in 2022 to 0.76 in 2025. Innovation capacity recorded the lowest mean value (0.45), suggesting that digital adoption does not automatically generate innovation. Inclusive development achieved a mean value of 0.52, reflecting gradual improvements in access to digital services and support systems. Theoretical/Methodological Contributions: The study demonstrates that digital modernization is most effective when supported by financial stability, institutional capacity, and access to economic opportunities, and proposes a multidimensional framework for evaluating digital transformation outcomes.

title: BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING REENGINEERING: ESSENCE AND IMPLEMENTATION FEATURES
summary: The purpose of the paper is to explore theoretical and applied aspects of outsourcing business process reengineering. The essence of reengineering is substantiated in the context of transferring non-core functions to external contractors, and key stages of process redesign, selection criteria for outsourcing partners, and integration mechanisms are defined. Methodology. The study employs methods of scientific generalization, structural-functional analysis, and process modeling to investigate the transformation of management systems. The research identifies core process stages, evaluation metrics (KPIs), stakeholder roles, potential risks, and control mechanisms through a systematic approach to business process optimization. Results of the study. The findings demonstrate that combining reengineering with outsourcing allows enterprises to optimize operating costs, accelerate operational cycles, improve service quality, and form an integrated business ecosystem capable of rapid adaptation to market changes. An integrated management model for outsourcing reengineering was developed, outlining six sequential stages from process diagnostics to continuous monitoring. Practical implications. The proposed reengineering program model and functional-process management mechanism can be utilized by enterprises across various industries seeking to enhance their competitiveness, reduce operational expenses, and streamline non-core functions during digital transformation and market instability. Value / originality. The paper provides a comprehensive theoretical and methodological framework for integrating business process reengineering and outsourcing, establishing a structured management model that bridges the gap between internal process optimization and external partnership coordination.

title: Transformasi Digital Administrasi Kepegawaian UIN Ar-Raniry Banda Aceh: Pengembangan Sistem Presensi Berbasis Web Menggunakan Metode Agile
summary: Digital transformation in personnel administration has become an urgent need in public higher education institutions, including at UIN Ar-Raniry Banda Aceh. This study aims to develop a web-based employee attendance system that can improve the efficiency, accuracy, and transparency of attendance recording and personnel administration processes. The research was conducted using the Human-Centered Design (HCD) approach and the Agile development method. The system was built using Java with the Spring Boot framework on the back-end, MongoDB as the database, and React.js on the front-end. The development focuses on three types of users: lecturers, permanent lecturers, and educational staff, with specific attention to different attendance location rules. The developed system includes several key features, namely GPS-based check-in and check-out attendance, an online application for leave and official duty, a finance menu that displays details of basic salary, net salary, deductions, remuneration, and meal allowance, as well as an interactive organizational structure visualization feature. All features were designed based on direct user feedback through an iterative HCD process. The development results show that the system is able to overcome the problems of manual attendance that have occurred so far and provides better transparency in personnel data management. This system is expected to serve as an initial step toward digital transformation of personnel administration at UIN Ar-Raniry Banda Aceh and can be replicated in other higher education institutions.

title: The CSR of football teams and its impact on the intention to purchase sponsors' products: a cross-cultural study
summary: Purpose This investigation aims to determine how football teams' corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities influence fan connection, including self-expression, identification, reputation and affective image, and how these factors affect fans' intentions to purchase sponsors' products. Additionally, this study explores the potential moderating effects of country, age, gender and team loyalty. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire was administered to 220 Colombian and 200 Spanish football fans. The data were analysed using structural equation modelling with the AMOS software. Findings The direct effect of team CSR on sponsor purchase intention was not significant, whereas the indirect effect through self-expression, team identification, team reputation and affective image was positive and significant. Country (Colombia vs Spain), age and gender did not moderate these relationships. Team loyalty did, but not by increasing the size of the effect: among highly loyal fans CSR reached sponsor patronage through the fan–team connection mediators, whereas among less loyal fans it operated directly. Loyalty therefore changes the route through which CSR reaches sponsor patronage rather than the total magnitude of its effect. Originality/value This study contributes to the sports marketing and CSR literature by testing a four-mediator model in a cross-cultural context and by identifying loyalty as a switch between relational and transactional processing of CSR signals. Because the two markets compared are culturally proximate, the observed stability should be understood as robustness within the Hispanic cultural sphere rather than as cultural universality. The study offers implications for teams and sponsors seeking to design communication strategies that optimise the return on CSR investment.

title: The dialectic of the carrot and the stick in the expansion of the extractive frontier in Oaxaca, Mexico
summary: • Introduces the dialectic of the carrot and the stick in extractive governance. • Corporate benefits produce differentiated and conditional forms of legitimacy. • Coercion changes the conditions under which opposition and accommodation occur. • Coercion and consent transform one another as extractive conflicts evolve. The expansion of large-scale mining in Mexico since the 1990s has been accompanied by intensifying socio-environmental conflicts, particularly in rural and Indigenous territories. While existing literature has shown that extractive governance frequently combines coercive practices with strategies aimed at securing local legitimacy, this article argues that these mechanisms are mutually constitutive rather than simply simultaneous or complementary. It develops the concept of the dialectic of the carrot and the stick to explain how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and coercion recursively reshape the conditions under which one another operate over the life of an extractive project. The article examines the San José silver and gold mine in Oaxaca, Mexico, operated by Fortuna Silver Mines (FSM). Drawing on qualitative fieldwork conducted between 2023 and 2024, including interviews, field observations, corporate publications, media reports, and civil society sources, it traces extractive governance over more than a decade of conflict. It shows that community programmes and relationships with local institutions produced differentiated and conditional forms of legitimacy, while repression, intimidation, and violence increased the costs of dissent and weakened resistance networks. Coercion thus transformed the terrain on which legitimacy was subsequently cultivated, while persistent limits to legitimacy generated renewed pressures to contain opposition. The dialectic therefore describes a recursive process through which coercion and consent reshape one another, enabling extraction to persist despite sustained opposition.

title: Capacidades digitales empresariales en empresas textiles de los Valles Centrales de Oaxaca
summary: This article analyzes the conceptual foundations and empirical evidence on the relationship between business digital capabilities and economic performance in order to develop a framework applicable to textile firms in the Central Valleys of Oaxaca. A documentary analysis of academic and institutional literature on digital transformation, dynamic capabilities, SME digitalization, business performance, and artisanal textile production is conducted. The literature distinguishes simple technology adoption from the organizational ability to select, integrate, use, and adapt digital resources in commercial and administrative processes. Based on this distinction, four analytical dimensions are proposed: digital commercial capability, digital management capability, information and data capability, and digital integration and adaptation capability. The reviewed evidence generally reports favorable associations between digitalization, digital capabilities, and several performance indicators; however, it also documents indirect, nonlinear, and context-dependent relationships shaped by skills, resources, strategic coherence, and digital maturity. Six territories are delimited for future empirical testing in the Central Valleys: Teotitlán del Valle, Santa Ana del Valle, San Miguel del Valle, San Pablo Villa de Mitla, Santo Tomás Jalieza, and San Antonino Castillo Velasco. The proposed model does not assume that the possession of social media accounts or digital tools automatically produces better economic results; rather, it argues that effects depend on the firm’s ability to embed digital resources in business routines and convert information, connectivity, and platforms into managerial and commercial action.

title: DIGITAL MATURITY OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: A METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH TO ASSESSMENT
summary: The article substantiates a methodological approach to assessing the digital maturity of public administration in environmental protection and natural resource management. Digital maturity is interpreted not as the number of electronic services but as the institutional capacity to use data, interoperable registers, geospatial technologies, analytical models and digital participation channels throughout the environmental policy cycle. A seven-dimensional model is proposed, covering institutional and strategic governance; data and interoperability; digital-by-design processes; platform integration; openness and participation; predictive analytics; and cyber resilience with human oversight. Five maturity levels and an aggregation method with a bottleneck rule are introduced to prevent strong components from concealing critical weaknesses. An information and analytical mechanism is developed that links environmental data sources, interoperability, analytics, managerial decisions, public interaction and ex post evaluation. Directions for applying the methodology in Ukraine are defined with regard to the EcoSystem platform, geospatial data infrastructure, the pollutant release and transfer register, digital environmental-impact assessment and environmental-monitoring reform. title: CONGLOMERATE GOVERNANCE: A STUDY OF THE ADANI PORTFOLIO
summary: The operational configuration of modern multi-layered infrastructure conglomerates possess a fascinating trilemma of capital formation and accumulation, regulatory compliance, and systemic risk management. This research considers the corporate ecosystem of the Adani Portfolio through an interdisciplinary perspective, examining how its specific 'incubator model' maintains the concentration of promoter's equity controlled by the S.B. Adani Family Trust as a response to the tough local market regulations enforced by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and international bond market disclosure rules. By analysing the portfolio's particular financial drivers, profit&loss metrics, and enterprise risk management frameworks, this research explores how large-scale utility corporations deal with cross-border informational shocks and geopolitical litigation challenges. Further, the research analyses the portfolio's infrastructural projects and developments to understand the combination of structural needs of corporate law, public-private partnerships (PPP), macroeconomic capital cycles, and mandatory ESG reporting frameworks and compliance to BRSR Keywords: Corporate Ecosystem, Enterprise Risk Management, Public-Private Partnerships, Macroeconomic Capital Cycles, ESG Reporting Frameworks.

title: IMPROVING THE MECHANISM FOR DEVELOPING COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES OF SMALL BUSINESSES IN THE DIGITAL ENVIRONMENT: THE CASE OF UZBEKISTAN.
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping the conditions under which small businesses compete and create value. This study examines the mechanism for developing competitive advantages among small businesses in the digital environment, with particular emphasis on digital capabilities, innovation, organizational flexibility, human capital, and market adaptation. The research combines theoretical analysis with an assessment of the current role of small businesses in Uzbekistan. Drawing on international experience and national conditions, the study proposes a conceptual mechanism that links digital resources to business process transformation, innovation, and competitive performance. The findings indicate that digitalization can generate sustainable competitive advantages when technological investments are supported by appropriate organizational capabilities and human capital.

title: Educating for Smart Governance: The CITAI_DATA Approach to Territorial Intelligence
summary: The establishment of CITAI_DATA – Center for Applied Intelligence, within the Department of Architecture, Arts and Design at ISMAT, aims to foster interdisciplinary innovation and digital transformation in territorial governance. The study presents the design and implementation of a new Executive Master focused on Smart Territories, integrating ethical, technological, and spatial dimensions. Methodologically, the program combines applied research, digital simulation, GeoAI, and data driven modeling to explore the social, environmental, and governance challenges of intelligent territories. The main results highlight the development of critical and technical competences in digital decision making, urban simulation, and responsible technological design. The study concludes that the program offers an integrated educational framework that aligns ethics, sustainability, and innovation, contributing to the formation of professionals capable of leading fair and data based territorial transformations.

title: A Kaizen perspective for managing human-technology continuous improvement in the digital age
summary: Purpose The paper examines how digital technologies are transforming continuous improvement (CI) by altering the cognitive and relational dynamics that have long underpinned Kaizen-oriented learning. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual approach, drawing on insights from CI, organizational learning and digital transformation. It establishes an interpretive framework focusing on cognitive offloading as a pivotal mechanism connecting technology adoption with the decline of participatory improvement routines. Findings Digital technologies can significantly speed up decision-making and streamline processes. However, there is a downside: their widespread use may reduce our ability to reflect, learn from experience and solve problems. When we start relying too much on technology for cognitive tasks, we risk becoming efficient in a procedural sense but socially vulnerable. This can weaken human skills that are essential for viable improvement. Practical implications The paper presents a conceptual model and practical guidelines for managers interested in developing CI systems that focus on maintaining discretion, fostering a strong learning environment and encouraging collective sense-making instead of merely optimizing execution. Originality/value Thanks to the adoption of Kaizen principles, the paper advances the discussion on CI by highlighting the fact that cognitive offloading poses a risk not only to individuals but also to organizations, particularly in environments that rely heavily on digital technology.

title: Mind the gaps! exploring the relationship between hierarchy and creative cognitive climate
summary: The role of hierarchy in organizations is under attack, particularly from those focused on organizational creativity and the digital transformation (DT). The call for flatter structures, reduced bureaucracy and network organizations, with the appropriate dispersion of authority, responsibility and power to achieve high levels of employee engagement, is the current rage. However, according to Elliot Jaques (1990), hierarchy itself is not to blame for our problems. He argued that we need an improved understanding of both hierarchy and human nature. The aim of hierarchy should be the improved deployment of human talent and energy. Despite attempts to reduce hierarchy in modern organizations, formal and informal hierarchies persist, in fact, even thrive in today’s DT environment. We investigated the relationship between creative cognitive climate at three levels of hierarchy: leaders, managers and staff. Exploring creative cognitive climate allowed for examining a deeper level of diversity. Using an assessment of these style differences across multiple industries and organizations, we found distinct gaps in collective style preferences across the three levels of stratification. Those at higher levels tended to prefer more novelty and less detailed structure and concern for authority. Those as lower levels tended to prefer novelty that fits the system and more structure and access to authority in dealing with their tasks. Based on these gaps, we identified four general and interrelated implications for improving communication, coordination, and collaboration across and within levels of various kinds of hierarchy.

title: BOD Characteristics and Sustainability Reporting in Zimbabwe, 2018
summary: This study examined how various board of directors (BOD) characteristics, including gender diversity, BOD ethnicity, BOD independence, and BOD size, influence sustainability reporting among organisations listed on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE). This study employed a positivist philosophical approach and an explanatory research design. The study population consisted of 64 organisations listed on the ZSE. Out of the 52 annual reports that were screened, 30 companies that reported on economic, social, environmental and governance issues were identified and used as a sample for the study. The researcher collected data from 40 top executives and 41 BOD members through a questionnaire and analysed it using regression to determine the relationship between selected BOD characteristics and sustainability reporting. The results show that only BOD ethnicity is statistically significantly and positively associated with sustainability reporting (β = .494, p < .05). In contrast, BOD size, BOD independence, and gender diversity show no statistically significant relationship. The research shows that board heterogeneity, especially BOD ethnicity, may enhance board effectiveness and encourage sustainability reporting by bringing diverse experience, perspectives, and relationships to board discussions. The study recommends that shareholders and corporate governance practitioners consider board diversity when appointing directors. Companies, meanwhile, should strengthen governance processes to enable diverse board members to contribute to sustainability reporting.

title: The impact of ESG ratings on corporate investment efficiency in a geopolitical context
summary: Purpose This paper examines the impact of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings on corporate investment efficiency amid rising geopolitical uncertainty, while uncovering the underlying transmission mechanisms and heterogeneous effects across firm types, thereby enriching the literature on ESG governance and corporate investment decision-making. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a multidimensional fixed-effects model for the baseline estimation. It further conducts heterogeneity tests based on firm lifecycle, technological attributes, and pollution levels, and examines the transmission channels, including financing constraints, green innovation, management costs, and managerial myopia. Findings Higher ESG ratings significantly reduce inefficient investments and enhance corporate investment efficiency. The positive effects are particularly pronounced in growth-stage, non-high-tech, and non-heavily polluting firms, while they are weaker in high-tech and declining firms. ESG ratings improve investment efficiency by alleviating financing constraints, promoting green innovation, reducing management costs, and mitigating managerial myopia. Originality/value This study links ESG ratings with corporate investment efficiency amid geopolitical uncertainty, thereby enriching the literature on the micro-level economic consequences of ESG practices and corporate investment decisions. It provides empirical evidence for firms to adopt differentiated ESG strategies to enhance investment efficiency and offers implications for policymakers in designing refined ESG governance frameworks in the context of global geopolitical and sustainable development competition.

title: The Impact of Digital Marketing and Delivery Speed on Customer Satisfaction at JNE Express
summary: Digital transformation and the increasing demand for faster services have made customer satisfaction in courier services dependent not only on the quality of digital interactions but also on delivery performance. This study aims to analyze the effects of digital marketing and delivery speed on customer satisfaction among JNE Express customers. A quantitative approach was employed through a survey of 130 JNE Express customers selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results show that digital marketing has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Delivery speed also has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect on customer satisfaction and explain more than half of the variation in customer satisfaction. These findings indicate that customer experience in courier services is shaped by a combination of relevant digital communication and the company's ability to fulfill service promises quickly and on time. Practically, companies need to integrate digital channel management with improvements in distribution process reliability to provide a more consistent customer experience.

title: Mapping knowledge management in Industry 4.0 era: a TCCM-guided bibliometric and thematic analysis
summary: This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management (KM) in the context of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory-Context-Characteristics-Method (TCCM) framework. Drawing on 93 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus (2018–2025), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM-based synthesis. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability (DKMC) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology-mediated capability shaped by human-AI interaction, real-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms. The study provides a transparent, theory-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments.

title: Disruptions in engineering academia: a systematic literature review
summary: Over the past decade, engineering academia has faced increasing disruptions stemming from global crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, and systemic shifts such as digital transformation and evolving labor markets. Despite the increasing prevalence of these disruptions, the literature remains fragmented in its definitions, typologies, and strategies for managing disruption in engineering education. This review investigates how disruptions in engineering academia have been defined, categorized, and managed between 2015 and 2024, with a focus on students, faculty, and institutional systems. Reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020, this systematic literature review searched Compendex and Inspec, accessed through Engineering Village, as well as ERIC and Web of Science. A total of 339 peer-reviewed studies were selected and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis to identify patterns in definitions, disruption types, and management strategies related to academic disruption. Most studies lacked explicit definitions of disruption, though thematic analysis revealed dominant framings of disruption as pandemic-induced shock, tech-driven change, and student experience breakdowns. Reported disruptions included shifts to online teaching, loss of hands-on learning, mental health strain, digital inequities, and institutional inflexibility. The most frequently reported management strategies were reconfiguring teaching and assessment, institutional coordination and policy adaptation, digital infrastructure investment, and equity-oriented student support. However, anticipatory or long-term strategic planning was rarely observed. The findings characterize disruption in engineering education as involving intertwined technological, structural, and socio-emotional dimensions. This review underscores the need for multi-level, inclusive, and resilience-oriented response that prioritizes adaptability, equity, and institutional readiness.

title: Dual Status Signaling and the Diffusion of Green Innovation
summary: This paper examines how status signaling shapes the diffusion of sustainable technologies. We develop an agent-based model that integrates two distinct forms of social status: conspicuous consumption, associated with traditional wealth-oriented prestige, and conspicuous conservation, reflecting the social value attached to visible sustainable choices. Heterogeneous consumers interact with strategically adapting firms that differentiate products along environmental and prestige dimensions. Calibrated to the German electric vehicles market, the model reproduces qualitative diffusion patterns and shows how diffusion accelerates when green innovations simultaneously signal material prestige and environmental values. The results further demonstrate how the effectiveness of this mechanism depends on structural conditions such as the income distribution and market structure.

title: Principal Component Analysis of Barriers to Smart Mining Technology Adoption in Hard-Rock Mining
summary: The transition toward smart mining technologies (SMTs), spanning automation, artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things and digital twins, is reshaping safety, productivity and sustainability outcomes across the global extractive sector. Yet, their adoption within South Africa’s hard-rock mining industry remains slow, fragmented and empirically under-theorised. Drawing on diffusion of innovation and socio-technical systems perspectives as interpretive lenses, this exploratory study investigates the barriers to SMT adoption as perceived by mining professionals. A quantitative research design was adopted, using a structured questionnaire administered to 80 mining professionals across South Africa’s Northwest, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces. Data were analysed through a three-stage process comprising reliability and validity testing, descriptive statistics, and principal component analysis (PCA). PCA of the twenty-one barriers identified in the literature extracted four components that jointly explained 62.05% of the total variance. Nineteen barriers met the loading criteria for assignment to these components: Adoption Risk and Workforce Barriers; Organisational and Stakeholder Readiness Barriers; Technological Awareness and Change Barriers; and Institutional and Environmental Sustainability Barriers. The findings suggest that, as perceived by the respondents, barriers to SMT adoption extend beyond technological limitations to include regulatory ambiguity, financial constraints, workforce readiness and weak institutional support. Given the modest, non-probability sample, the component structure is exploratory and preliminary. It requires confirmatory testing in larger, independent samples before it is extended to other capital-intensive, safety-critical and regulation-heavy industries. The study concludes with practical, policy, and theoretical implications for mining firms, technology providers, regulators, and researchers seeking to accelerate safe, sustainable, and intelligent digital transformation.

title: Campus-Wide ICT Infrastructure and E-Learning Integration Project
summary: Executive Overview This document presents an independent institutional infrastructure proposal titled "Campus-Wide ICT Infrastructure and E-Learning Integration Project," developed as a strategic intervention model for Kaduna Polytechnic (Kaduna State, Nigeria). Designed to bridge the digital divide and modernize instructional delivery, this proposal outlines a comprehensive technical framework for expanding campus-wide broadband access, establishing modern e-learning ecosystems, and upgrading institutional digital infrastructure to support blended learning. Scope & Technical Framework The proposed intervention covers three core modernization pillars: 1. Campus Network Backbone & Broadband Expansion: Deployment of modern fiber-optic local area networks (LAN), high-density campus Wi-Fi access points, core server room upgrades, and redundant power backups for ICT hubs. 2. E-Learning Platform & Digital Resource Integration: Enterprise deployment of an open-source Learning Management System (LMS), digital library integration, multimedia smart classroom equipment, and virtual lab simulation tools. 3. Digital Capacity Building & Literacy: Comprehensive training modules for academic staff on digital pedagogy, e-content development, LMS administration, and technical support protocols for ICT staff. Financial & Operational Architecture · Proposed Beneficiary Institution: Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria · Target Supervising Units: Directorate of Information & Communication Technology (DICT) / Computer Center / Library Services · Project Implementation Window: 6 Months · Total Estimated Budget: ₦145,000,000 / $95,000 equivalent · Target Funding Mechanism: UNESCO (Regional Office, Abuja / Education Sector) Purpose & Open-Access Availability This repository item is published as an open-access policy and infrastructure design artifact. It serves as a structural template for researchers, institutional developers, and funding agencies interested in digital transformation, e-learning adoption, and ICT infrastructure expansion in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions across Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Greenwashing and Directors' Liability under the Companies Act, 2013: An Analysis of Directors' Duties in ESG Governance
summary: Greenwashing is a major concern for corporate governance as firms communicate environmental performance through sustainability reports, ESG disclosures and advertisements. It occurs when a company's environmental claims are false, misleading, exaggerated, vague or insufficiently supported by evidence. This study examines when directors can be held liable for greenwashing under the Companies Act, 2013, with reference to their statutory and fiduciary duties. The study focuses on Section 166 and also examines Sections 134, 149(12), 447 and 448, SEBI's BRSR and BRSR Core framework and the CCPA Guidelines, 2024. It is doctrinal and analytical, with a comparative study of the EU, UK, US and Australia. It finds that Indian law offers several mechanisms against greenwashing, but no comprehensive framework determines when it leads to personal director liability, and recommends stronger board-level ESG oversight, verification of sustainability information and better regulatory coordination.
